thread:
Jonah: heads-up — after the routing policy flip to cost-first at ~08:15, we're seeing a surge in tool-invoke rejects tied to structured-output validation
Maria: saw that too. rejects are `schema_mismatch` and `missing_required` mostly. counts jumped ~8x in the last 30m
Sam: do we know if it's a model variant mismatch (returns an array vs object) or our validator tightened? can we get a raw example for an alerting rule
Jonah: here's one raw sample from the console quarantine feed (redacted):
```
{\"tool\":\"price_lookup\",\"result\":\[{\"price\":null}\],\"meta\":{}}
```
Maria: result should be an object {price: number}, model returned array; that triggers strict validator
Tess: this is classic routing fallout — cheaper model variant returns different shape. we didn't pin schema compatibility in the cost-first policy
Sam: ok, two prongs: (1) telemetry: we need a reject-level sample exposed in the dashboard with anonymized payloads, not just counts. (2) routing: fallback to compat model when we detect shape mismatch
Jonah: suggested dashboard fields: timestamp, route_policy, model_variant, reject_code, example_snippet, request_id
Maria: + a histogram of time-to-detect (from invoke -> reject) and example rate of false positives after retries
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for route-fallbacks v2 at 2026-03-20T09:40:00Z
Sam: small UX ask: console should let SREs re-run a sample against another variant from the UI (run-with-variant button). helps triage quickly
Tess: agree. also need quota implications — repeated retries bump up token usage and costs. add a metric: retry_tokens_burned_by_rejects
Jonah: for short-term mitigation, can we flip the policy to prefer strict-compat models for production namespaces and keep cost-first on dev
Maria: we can, but want automated detection first. propose: if reject_rate_by_route > 1% AND reject_type == schema_mismatch for 5m, auto-pin compat variant for that route for 10m
Sam: sounds reasonable. add a TTL and a manual override in console
Tess: open question: sampling rate for capturing payloads — we can't store every rejected payload. propose 1% global sampling + deterministic sampling by request_id hash for high-severity customers
Maria: agreed. also add allowlist for enterprise customers (no sampling unless allowed) for compliance
Jonah: action items:
- Sam: add reject_sample stream + UI column (dashboard PR)
- Tess: implement auto-pin policy with TTL + manual override
- Maria: add metric retry_tokens_burned_by_rejects and alert when > threshold
- infra-bot: annotate canary rollout and rollback window
Sam: i'll start the dashboard PR, will include example snippet preview with redaction and a quick link to re-run
Tess: i'll draft the auto-pin RFC and put it behind a canary flag
Maria: i'll add the metric to our billing telemetry pipeline and a simple playbook entry
Jonah: thanks — let's sync again in 30m if counts don't drop. :thumbsup:
